definition: Despot means a ruler who holds total power and governs harshly.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word despot. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know despot should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The old duke governed as a despot: taxes rose at his whim, judges served at his pleasure, and no one dared print a word about either.
A premier is the mildest figure here, nowhere near a despot: a premier holds power on a lease — one lost vote in the assembly and the whole cabinet goes home.
Autocrat goes further than premier — no vote can reach him; despot claims the most: the same unanswerable power, used as a whip.

A tyrant is defined by cruelty: the word leads with the suffering he causes, whatever the legal shape of his rule. A despot leads with the totality of the power itself — every check gone — and the harshness follows behind. The two meet in the same throne room by different doors.

A dictator is a ruler who has seized total control of a modern state, often by coup, and the word points at the route to power as much as the holding of it. A despot may inherit his throne quite legally; what marks him is how he rules once seated — alone, and harshly.

Despotes came into English in one piece, and its ancient parts — a house-word and a master-word — made no other English word between them. Learn the picture instead: a whole country run like one man's household.
Despot means a ruler who holds total power and governs harshly.
When the emira of Qaresh died in 1902, her son dismissed the council of forty families within a month.
He alone signed the port ledgers, he alone chose the garrison's officers, and complaint became a crime tried in his own chambers.
Merchants bribed; farmers hid their grain; nobody voted, because the despot had left nothing to vote on.
Despot is the exact word for the son, because a despot is a ruler who holds total power and governs harshly — both halves required.
An autocrat also rules alone, and the word stops there; despot adds the heavy hand.
His mother had ruled alone too, and gently, which is why the chronicles call her an autocrat and him something worse.
